articles.title: Ontario education ministry alleges thousands of OSAP applications came from single IP address
articles.summary: At two career colleges now under the Ontario government's microscope, more than half of the thousands of student financial aid applications last year came from a single IP address, officials allege…

image.caption: Newly filed allegations against Academy of Learning schools come as Premier Doug Ford's government is under increasing fire for its handling of OSAP. Opposition parties recently called for the firing of Ontario Minister of Colleges and Universities Nolan Quinn, pictured here during question period t

blocks.text: At two career colleges now under the Ontario government's microscope, more than half of the thousands of student financial aid applications last year came from a single IP address, officials allege in documents filed in court.

The government has also received more than 200 tips about that network of schools, including allegations that certain recruiters were submitting students' Ontario Student Assistance Program (OSAP) applications at those schools, which is not allowed, and completing their coursework, those same documents show.

The Academy of Learning did not provide comment on the new court filings in response to a request from The Canadian Press, but has previously denied allegations of wrongdoing. They say the schools have implemented a long list of corrective actions, including cutting ties with some recruiters and bolstering admissions practices. The ministry's allegations have not been proven in court.

The newly filed allegations against the schools come as Premier Doug Ford's government is under increasing fire for its handling of OSAP. Critics say alleged misuse of the system was allowed to fester under lax oversight, then when it was brought to light Ford left innocent students paying the price.
Ontario extends OSAP freeze for private colleges into the new year

Colleges and Universities Minister Nolan Quinn says his government acted on tips and conducted in-depth inspections that ultimately led to barring the schools from OSAP eligibility and launching a broader probe.

Quinn earlier this year drastically reduced the amount of OSAP grants that students at universities and publicly funded colleges could receive in the name of "sustainability" as the program was facing rising costs.
Those costs were later revealed by The Canadian Press to largely be due to activity at a small number of career colleges.
Between 2023-24 and 2024-25, the amount of provincial OSAP grants to career colleges nearly doubled, to about $1 billion in the latter year.

items: Students left stranded as Ontario halts OSAP funding for private colleges

blocks.text: The Academy of Learning operates as franchises but the three schools barred from OSAP share a parent company, Opulence Education Group. Its campuses in Toronto on Bay Street and in North York, and one in Brampton East, accounted for one-fifth of that spending.

The three schools were among six that in May the province made ineligible for OSAP, citing an "inability to reliably determine bona fide studies," a decision the schools are challenging in court. As part of that case, the province issued a final decision in August and added that to the court record in October.

"The ministry is not satisfied that the institutions have adequate processes in place to ensure that its records and processes can be relied on for the proper administration and disbursement of OSAP funding to eligible students," the decision says.

Ministry officials who last year inspected the campuses at issue looked at a sampling of student accounts and found evidence of shared IP address activity across students referred by the same recruiter, the government alleges.
Shared IP addresses do not mean misconduct: school group
In completing its final decision to deny the schools OSAP eligibility this year, the ministry appears to have taken a closer look at IP address activity.

There were 6,001 OSAP applications from students at the Brampton East campus for the 2025-26 year and 3,136 of them — 52 per cent — came from a single IP address, the ministry alleges. There were five more IP addresses responsible for 100 or more applications, they allege.

At the North York campus, 3,460 out of 6,070 OSAP applications for that year — 57 per cent — came from a single IP address, the ministry alleges. Two other IP addresses were responsible for another 255 applications, they allege.

The Bay campus saw 6,966 OSAP applications that year, with 1,736 — 25 per cent — coming from a single IP address, the ministry alleges. Five other IP addresses submitted 100 or more applications, they allege.
The Academy of Learning argued in an earlier letter to the ministry that shared IP addresses may be due to multiple people living at the same address, but the ministry is calling that into question.

items: Ontario refers OSAP concerns at private career colleges to provincial police
Ontario delayed OSAP inspections at 2 career colleges: court records

blocks.text: "While patterns of shared IP addresses among students attending the same physical school campus space accessing their student accounts may be expected, patterns of shared IP address activity among the institution's asynchronous learners referred to the institution by the same recruiter is significant and renders the institution's proposed explanation unlikely in this case," the ministry wrote in the court filing.

In its letter to the province to rebut any nefarious assumptions about students' logins, the Academy of Learning also wrote, "the presence of the same IP address among different users does not, by itself, establish misconduct, misrepresentation, or unauthorized activity."

Quinn has tasked KPMG with an audit of OSAP payments to career colleges and in October referred the matter to the Ontario Provincial Police, while pausing such payments to all private post-secondary institutions. It is not known if the referral contains specific allegations relating to the Academy of Learning.
It comes after warnings from Career Colleges Ontario, the federal government, and hundreds of tips and complaints about possible misuse of the OSAP system.
Ministry received over 200 tips about school group

The new ministry court filings reveal that since Jan. 1, 2024, it has received more than 220 tips, complaints, referrals and investigations relating to the three Academy of Learning campuses, with the volume and consistency of the concerns "significant," the government alleges.

"The ministry received related third-party complaints and tips alleging that certain recruiters were acting on behalf of students, including in submitting OSAP applications, in uploading supporting documentation on students' OSAP accounts, and in completing coursework on behalf of students, and that recruiters were using OSAP funding as a recruitment or marketing tool," the ministry wrote.
The schools have since cut off ties with some recruiters, they have said.

Academy of Learning did not directly respond to a request for comment by The Canadian Press on the allegation that recruiters were completing students' coursework, but has noted in a corrective action plan last year that it added enhanced IP tracking to identify possible third-party access and added two-factor authentication "to safeguard against third-party completion of assignments."
Liberals demand audit into private college OSAP spending

NDP critic Peggy Sattler said given all the information that is now public about what the government knew or should have known about the skyrocketing OSAP usage at some career colleges, it is shocking they did not act with more urgency.

"I think the more details that we learn through these court proceedings, the clearer it is that the minister was completely incompetent at doing his job," she said. "It is stunning that these five-alarm fires were being ignored by the government."
Liberal critic Tyler Watt also said the new revelations reflect poorly on Quinn.

items: Ontario blocks 3 career colleges from OSAP until at least 2030

blocks.text: "Minister Nolan Quinn keeps insisting he's taken this scandal seriously, but every new revelation raises more questions about what his ministry knew, when they knew it, and why they failed to act," he wrote in a statement.
Quinn's office said when serious concerns are identified, they do not hesitate to cut an institution off from OSAP entirely, as was done with the Academy of Learning locations in this court case.
"Any misuse of OSAP is unacceptable," Bianca Giacoboni wrote in a statement. "We have zero tolerance for bad actors who threaten the integrity of our post-secondary system."
Quinn has indicated he will introduce further legislation this fall to enhance accountability in the system.

articles.title: Oil price falls amid hope of a breakthrough to end Iran war
articles.summary:
Brent crude drops by more than 6% to $105.55 a barrel, the lowest level in more than two weeks

The oil price has fallen to its lowest level in more two weeks amid new hopes of a breakthrough…

blocks.text: The oil price has fallen to its lowest level in more two weeks amid new hopes of a breakthrough to end the Iran war.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, dropped by more than 6.5% to as low as $105.55 a barrel on Monday, the lowest since 16 October, sending shares in airline companies higher and pushing down government borrowing costs.
Oil prices fell after Tehran revealed that contacts between Iran and the US to end their eight-month war were continuing.

“Consultations through mediators are very ⁠intensive. We have presented our conditions and ⁠proposals and everything depends on the political ​rationality of Washington,” the Iranian foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, said, according to the state media outlet IRNA.
Over the weekend, Qatari officials tried to negotiate the release of more than $6bn (£4.5bn) in Iranian assets, so that Tehran might allow the strait of Hormuz to reopen.
Donald Trump had earlier taken a belligerent tone, telling voters in Iowa on Sunday that Iran would receive “the hammer” unless there was progress.

“The only reason why I’m not finished with Iran is I want to be nice. I want to try and save all those lives if I can ... But at some point we’re going to have to give them the hammer,” he said during a campaign rally in the run-up to the US midterm elections.
But investors were cheered by reports on Monday that Iran’s supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, had granted “powers” to his government in its talks with the US seeking to end the Middle East war.

Chris Beauchamp, the chief market analyst at the investing and trading platform IG, said: “The news is manna from heaven for stock markets, which have felt increasingly pressured by oil’s rise, but of course there is still a risk that Trump will try one last throw of the iron dice after the midterms.”
after newsletter promotion

The drop in the oil price sparked hopes of a break in the inflationary pressures gripping the global economy. Government borrowing costs dropped, with the yield – or interest rate – on 10-year UK bonds down 10 basis points, or 0.1 of a percentage point, to the lowest since 22 September.
Shares in British Airways’ parent company, IAG, rose by 4.2% in London, while United Airlines jumped 7% in New York.

articles.title: Martha Stewart says she 'really screwed up' after posting homeless Halloween costume
articles.summary: Martha Stewart has issued a second apology after she shared a photo of herself in a Halloween costume widely criticized as mocking people experiencing homelessness.

image.caption: Multi-millionaire lifestyle mogul Martha Stewart is facing heated backlash after sharing a photo over the weekend of a Halloween costume that has been widely criticized as mocking homeless people. (Andy Kropa/Invision/The Associated Press and Martha Stewart/Instagram)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New
Martha Stewart has issued a second apology after she shared a photo of herself in a Halloween costume widely criticized as mocking people experiencing homelessness.
The millionaire lifestyle mogul has been subject to scathing criticism after now-deleted post

The multi-millionaire, known for building a massive food and lifestyle empire, posted a photo of herself on Instagram over the weekend with a dirt-streaked face and ripped clothes, holding a sign that read, "I AM HUNGRY. HELP ME!!"
The post was swiftly deleted, but not before internet users had grabbed screenshots of the costume, sharing it widely on social media, where it stirred up disbelief and fury.
"The level of out of touch is stellar," one Reddit user wrote.
"Rich people never cease to amaze me with their callousness," another chimed in.
Many called it a real-life "let them eat cake," moment, referencing the infamous myth that queen consort of France, Marie Antoinette, said this when told the peasants had no bread to eat.

The controversy comes amid a worsening cost-of-living crisis in the U.S. — a recent survey found that 47 per cent of Americans reported financial problems from rising prices, up from 30 per cent in 2025, according to PBS.
This image, shared in a carousel to Stewart's personal Instagram account, @marthastewart48, was quickly deleted after it began to spark furious backlash. (Instagram/Martha Stewart)
As the backlash grew, Stewart issued a statement Sunday on her Instagram.

"It's hard to admit when you've really screwed up," she wrote. "My earlier statement didn't go far enough. I know many people are suffering economically. Wearing a costume like I did was insensitive and not funny. I am very sorry."
It was her second apology, after her first attempts at addressing the wave of anger went poorly.

Earlier on Sunday, after entertainment outlet JustJared made a post about the criticism, the 85-year-old Stewart had left a comment, claiming that she had only wanted to raise awareness about homelessness.

"My costume was designed to bring the homeless and the hungry to everyone's mind and boy it certainly did!!! But not in the correct way, because I did not explain it and I am so sorry I care and I support causes who care. Do all of you???" she wrote.

Stewart, shown here preparing a breakfast frittata in a 2020 file photo, was the first U.S. self-made female billionaire, earning that title in 2000. Her current net worth is around $400 million US. (Cindy Ord/Getty Images)

Her critics weren't buying it. Some replies pointed out that the costume was offensive regardless of intent, and others noted Stewart hadn't mentioned awareness at all in her original post — which had used the caption to plug candles she had for sale on home-shopping network QVC instead.
Actress Indya Moore, known for the TV series Pose, was one of those calling out Stewart's actions.

"Halloween is caricature: monsters, villains, idols. People do not dress up as groups who are in crisis," she wrote in an Instagram story. "If you were serious about poverty, you'd use your platform to back policies that tax the rich, put free food in front of people who are hungry and homeless, and provide free health care and education."

items: Canadian food bank use hits 2.3 million monthly visits due to grocery costs: report
Some Canadians are crowdfunding their way through the cost of living crisis
Why living alone is becoming increasingly unaffordable for Torontonians

blocks.text: Moore shared a list of charity organizations, suggesting Stewart consider supporting them with her vast wealth of resources.

"I really feel like the culture around wealth and making money is so deeply interwoven with shaming people who are poor, who are struggling financially and economically, and it's so disturbing," she said in a followup video.

Stewart, who has an estimated net worth of $400 million US, lives primarily at her 150-acre estate in Katonah, New York, known as Cantitoe Corners or Bedford Farm. Purchased in 2000 for $15.6 million, according to People magazine, it is one of several properties Stewart owns.
Stewart arrives for the launch of 2023's Sports Illustrated swimsuit issue in New York City on May 18, 2023. (Jeenah Moon/Reuters)

There are around 145,500 people experiencing homelessness in New York state, according to the state's latest figures. More than 30 per cent of them are children, double the rate of the rest of the U.S.
In Canada, around 65,000 people experience homelessness on a given night across 75 Canadian communities, according to a 2025 report.
Stewart's second apology has left many still skeptical. Negative comments have hit her brand's official Instagram, as well.
Under one post plugging a new recipe, one user wrote, "No martha … you can't maple cake your way out of this."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Alexandra Mae Jones is a senior writer for CBC News based in Toronto. She has written on a variety of topics, from health to pop culture to breaking news, and previously reported for CTV News and the Toronto Star. She joined CBC in 2024. You can reach her at alexandra.mae.jones@cbc.ca

articles.title: Poland's in the midst of a constitutional crisis. Here's what's happening
articles.summary: A decade-long dispute in Poland over one of its top courts has come to a head, with the country's prime minister and president at loggerheads, and protests outside the Constitutional Tribunal in…

image.caption: Right-wing supporters hold the Polish flag and shout slogans during a standoff between the Polish government and the Constitutional Tribunal's top judges in Warsaw on Saturday. (Getty Images)

blocks.text: World

A decade-long dispute in Poland over one of its top courts has come to a head, with the country's prime minister and president at loggerheads, and protests outside the Constitutional Tribunal in Warsaw flaring this weekend. Here's why.
Long-running political dispute over judicial independence has effectively paralyzed constitutional court

A decade-long dispute in Poland over one of its top courts has come to a head over the last two weeks, with the country's prime minister and president at loggerheads, and protests outside the Constitutional Tribunal in Warsaw flaring this weekend.
Here's what's happening and why.
Crisis began with right-wing victory, court control
The Constitutional Tribunal is responsible for checking the compatibility of laws, policies and international agreements with the national constitution.
It has been a major bone of contention between the current pro-European government and the main opposition party, national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS).

PiS drastically transformed the country’s justice system after winning election in 2015, including establishing political control over top courts such as the Constitutional Tribunal and the Supreme Court. This was done in part by cancelling the appointments of judges selected by the previous government and choosing its own.
Back in 2016, opponents of Law and Justice protested outside the building shouting "Democracy!" and "Constitution!"

The European Union’s top court ruled in December 2025 that the Constitutional Tribunal was not "independent and impartial," because of politicized appointments made by the since-defeated Law and Justice government. The EU withheld billions of euros in funds to Poland during the nationalist PiS-led governments of 2015 to 2023, saying their judiciary reforms had subverted democratic checks and balances.
Pro-EU government promises to reform court
After Donald Tusk's pro-European coalition took office ​in 2023, it pledged to restore the rule of law and reform the court.

But President Karol Nawrocki, a Law and Justice ally, has acted to thwart those ⁠efforts since his election as president in 2025. Earlier this year, Nawrocki refused to swear in several judges nominated by parliament.

Meanwhile, the tribunal's chief judge, Bogdan Swieczkowski, a former deputy justice minister in the Law and Justice administration, declined to seat judges elected by the current parliamentary majority.
Constitutional Tribunal president Bogdan Swieczkowski speaks with protesters gathered outside the court's headquarters in Warsaw, Poland, on Oct. 30. (Wojtek Radwanski/AFP/Getty Images)
Chief judge suspended

A statement appeared on the tribunal's website on Friday saying Swieczkowski had been suspended. "Restoring the rule of law is our obligation," Prime Minister Tusk wrote on X on Friday evening. "After years of lawlessness under PiS this is a difficult process, sometimes painful and it requires decisive action. There is no other way."
Speaking on Saturday night, Tusk compared PiS to a man who steals an elderly woman’s purse and then claims to be the victim when police catch him and take it back.
Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk, centre, in Brussels on Oct. 15. (Nicolas Tucat/The Associated Press)
"I am certain that the Constitutional Tribunal will function as it ​should," he said in a televised speech. "Also, independently of me and in line with the constitution.
"The task of the executive branch, and therefore mine, is to ensure its ​safety and working conditions, and I intend to fulfil my duty."
How PiS and its supporters have responded

Protesters gathered outside the tribunal on Friday and Saturday night in response, and Nawrocki turned back his plane during a flight to Senegal and returned home. He made his way to the Constitutional Tribunal early Saturday despite the chaos.

"Tonight, there was a breach of public order in the Republic of Poland and a forcible takeover of a ⁠constitutional body," Nawrocki said in a statement read by an aide outside the court early on Saturday, where several hundred protesters gathered.
Protesters called for Swieczkowski's re-instatement and accused the government of carrying out a coup.

Police, who have been guarding the court since Friday afternoon, said they detained three protesters on Friday night after some threw objects at officers and tried to break through the security fence around the court.
What's at stake
The government is a broad coalition made up of Tusk's centrist Civic Coalition, the Left and two more conservative groupings, Poland 2050 and the Polish People's Party, or PSL.
Representatives of Poland 2050 and PSL, along with several opposition parties, met with Nawrocki on Saturday, while Tusk did not attend.
The president's camp is hoping that the crisis surrounding the Constitutional Tribunal will erode Tusk's parliamentary majority.

items: Poland formally withdraws from Ottawa Convention on landmines, citing Russian threat
How, and at what cost, could Canada catch up to Poland's defence spending?

blocks.text: A general assembly of Constitutional Tribunal judges is scheduled for Tuesday, but its ability to make decisions will depend on securing a ‌quorum of 10 of the court's 15 judges.
The latest events took place a year before Poland's next parliamentary election, when Tusk's pro-European coalition will face several hard-right parties who support the president's position.

How it plays out over the coming days or weeks could have a significant impact on next year's parliamentary election and potentially push Poland away from the European ‌mainstream and closer to U.S. President Donald Trump.
With files from Reuters and The Associated Press

articles.title: Duterte ICC trial: Victims face language barriers, concerns over scope of charges
articles.summary: Drug war victims face challenges in participating meaningfully in the ICC trial, including language barriers, witness protection concerns, and questions over the scope of charges.

blocks.text: THE HAGUE, Netherlands — Victims of alleged crimes committed during former president Rodrigo Duterte's war on drugs face challenges in participating meaningfully in his upcoming trial before the International Criminal Court (ICC), including language barriers, witness protection concerns, and questions over the scope of charges.

Among the key concerns raised during the court's fifth status conference on Monday, November 2, was an ICC decision that could limit the killings covered by the case, potentially excluding some victims from the proceedings.
The conference also addressed preparations for Duterte's trial, scheduled to open on November 30, including witness protection measures and arrangements for victims' participation.
In an interview, attorney Kristina Conti, an ICC Assistant to Counsel, said these issues remain significant for victims as the proceedings approach.
Change in scope of charges raises concerns for victims
Conti said victims' representatives are grappling with the implications of an ICC decision issued on October 9 that appears to limit the scope of killings covered by one of the charges.

The case concerns alleged crimes committed between November 1, 2011, and March 16, 2019, when the Philippines was a member of the ICC. However, the decision reportedly limits the killings covered by one charge to the period between July 1, 2016, and September 30, 2018.
“Yung tinatawag na paglimita ng scope ang problema ngayon ng mga biktima kasi posibleng hindi lahat, eh, pumasok doon sa parameters,” Conti told GMA News Online.
(The limitation of the scope is now a problem for victims because some of them may not fall within the parameters of the case.)

Conti said victims' representatives are still trying to understand the implications of the ruling, arguing that the alleged crimes should be considered within the full period of the Philippines' membership in the ICC.
“Dapat hanggang 2019 na miyembro yung Pilipinas ng ICC. Tapos dapat hanggang 2022 kung kailan tsaka pa lang natapos yung term ni Duterte,” she said.
(It should cover when the Philippines was a member of the ICC, until 2019. And Duterte's term only ended in 2022.)
The potential narrowing of the scope is a concern for victims who fear that not all alleged crimes may be considered in the proceedings.
Participating victims need not testify

Conti clarified that victims participating in the proceedings do not necessarily have to take the witness stand. Their role is to express their views and concerns through their common legal representatives and, potentially, seek reparations if Duterte is convicted.
She stressed that the number of participating victims does not determine the strength of the prosecution's evidence.

“Yung pagliit o paglaki ng bilang na ito ay hindi nakakaapekto directly doon sa kaso or doon sa strength ng evidence. Pero siyempre, ibang tulong din yun na alam ng prosecution, makikita nila na ganito karami ang gustong mag-participate,” she said.

(The increase or decrease in the number of participating victims does not directly affect the case or the strength of the evidence. But, of course, it also helps the prosecution to see how many people want to participate.)
Conti encouraged victims to participate even if they are unwilling or unable to testify, submit affidavits, or recount their experiences in court.

“Pero gusto pa rin sana namin na anyayahan sila na mag-participate. Not necessarily para maging witness, not necessarily para magbigay ng statement na kumbaga affidavit, pero para magbigay ng views and concerns, mga pananaw at mga agam-agam,” she said.
(We still want to encourage them to participate. Not necessarily as witnesses, and not necessarily to submit affidavits, but to share their views and concerns.)
Applications from participating victims will continue to be accepted until the prosecution finishes presenting its evidence, Conti said.
The prosecution has been allotted 150 hours to present its evidence, a phase she estimates could take approximately a year.
Victims' safety and participation
Conti said preparations for the November 30 trial were largely in place, with the court emphasizing protective measures for witnesses who will testify either in person or through audio-visual links.
“Pero yung maganda nga dito na na-emphasize ay yung protective measures para sa witnesses,” she said.
(What was particularly good was the emphasis on protective measures for witnesses.)
These measures could include withholding witnesses' identities and preventing them from appearing on screen if the ICC determines that revealing their identities could put them at risk.
“Posibleng hindi rin natin makita sa screen. Posibleng boses lang ang marinig natin o kaya translated voice,” said Conti.
(We may not even see them on screen. We may hear only their voice, or a translated voice.)
She said protecting victims and witnesses is particularly important given the trauma they may experience when recounting alleged abuses.
Filipino language request faces hurdles
Another issue raised by victims' representatives was the request to use Filipino during portions of the proceedings, particularly when reading statements directly from victims.
Conti said the request was not simply about language preference but about allowing victims to hear their experiences conveyed in their own words.
“Hindi sila magsasalita ng Tagalog simple dahil gusto nila, kundi dahil meron silang i-quote o babasahin na statement diretso directly from the victims,” she said.
(They are not asking to speak in Tagalog simply because they want to, but because they intend to quote or read statements directly from the victims.)
However, the request appears unlikely to be granted, meaning statements would have to be delivered in English or translated.
Conti said this would not affect the legal merits of the case but could influence victims' perception of whether they are genuinely included in the proceedings.
“Pero yung impression lang sa Pilipinas, yung participation ng victims. Kumbaga eh, isinali niyo na nga kami... Pero kailangan pala English dito,” she said.
(But it affects the impression in the Philippines about victims' participation. It's as if we're being told, ‘You've included us, but everything has to be in English.’)
She warned that the English-language requirement could discourage some victims from participating, particularly those without immediate access to lawyers or legal representatives.

“Isa siyang malaking barrier—lalo na sa iba na hindi naman naaabot kaagad nung CLRV o kaya nakakapag-consult agad sa mga abogado, so baka maiwan sila sa proseso o hindi nila maintindihan ang nangyayari.”

(It is a significant barrier, especially for those who cannot immediately reach a common legal representative or consult a lawyer. They could be left behind in the process or may not understand what is happening.)

Duterte's trial is scheduled to begin on November 30. He faces three counts of crimes against humanity in connection with alleged killings during his administration's anti-drug campaign. — BM, GMA News

articles.title: U.S. federal investigators to provide update after Florida plane crash that killed 9

image.caption: First responders attend the scene of a deadly plane crash in Palm Beach County, Fla., on Sunday. The crash, which killed nine people, is being investigated by federal officials. (Mark Elias/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New

A business jet crashed into a South Florida neighbourhood and erupted into a ball of flames, killing all nine people on board and leaving a fiery crater. The cause was not immediately clear, but federal investigators are expected to provide an update at 1 p.m. ET on Monday.
Officials have not yet identified those on board the Bahamas-bound aircraft
A business jet crashed into a South Florida neighbourhood and erupted into a ball of flames, killing all nine people on board and leaving a fiery crater.

The cause was not immediately clear, but federal investigators are expected to provide an update during a news conference at 1 p.m. ET on Monday in West Palm Beach. CBC News will be carrying it live here.

Video recorded by passersby captured the terrifying moment on Sunday afternoon, when the Bahamas-bound aircraft plunged from the sky before slamming into the ground and exploding in Green Acres, about 11 kilometres southwest of West Palm Beach. Flames flickered around chunks of pavement lining the crater as shocked residents looked on in horror. Thick black smoke engulfed the crash site.

"Debris was everywhere. Debris hit my house. Everything was on fire. The road was on fire," Anthony Blackmon, who lives near the crash site, told NBC affiliate WTVJ. "I've always seen it on the news, never thought it would happen so close to somebody, like how it happened today."
Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said there were no immediate reports of anyone on the ground injured or killed. Authorities have not yet released the names of the people who died.

items: All 9 aboard killed after plane crashes in Florida, officials say

blocks.text: Palm Beach County authorities were evacuating about 600 people from a nearby mobile home community while the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) investigate the crash.
Authorities have not provided any information about what caused the Bahamas-bound Learjet 60 to crash.

The jet began its journey at the Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas, and airport spokesperson Jim Reynolds described it as a private aircraft. He could not immediately provide details about who was on board.
The plane was heading east at about 35,000 feet when the pilot started to report problems.

The pilot said ice was accumulating on the jet and that turbulence was jolting it by as much as 700 feet (210 metres), according to air traffic control recordings captured by LiveATC.net. Rain pounded the region on Sunday.
"We have light, clear ice that is manageable and moderate turbulence," the pilot told controllers.
The situation rapidly deteriorated.
Jet lost altitude at alarming rate
The pilot requested permission to climb another 2,000 feet (610 metres), then quickly declared an emergency as the jet lost altitude at an alarming rate.
"We're descending 8,000 — mayday, mayday — we're descending 10,000 feet per minute," the pilot radioed.

"We are in an overspeed condition, descending 20,000 feet per minute," the pilot radioed, before delivering a devastating acknowledgment of what was about to happen. "We're going to crash into the ground."
Mayday call captures final moments before Florida jet crash
The plane banked sharply to the right before crashing and exploding.
"It was a cataclysmic plane crash," DeSantis told reporters at the scene. "It looked like a missile going down and left a big crater on the side of the road."

articles.title: PH, Indonesia seek to deepen ties under 5-year action plan
articles.summary: The Philippines and Indonesia reaffirmed their commitment to boost bilateral ties, including cooperation on maritime security, economic relations and border management.

blocks.text: Published November 3, 2026 12:11am
The Philippines and Indonesia reaffirmed their commitment to boost bilateral ties, including cooperation on maritime security, economic relations and border management.

Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro and Indonesia's new Foreign Minister Arrmanatha “Tata” Christiawan Nasir met in Manila on Monday during the Indonesian diplomat's introductory visit following his appointment as the country's top diplomat last month, the DFA said.

The two officials discussed progress in bilateral relations, citing the Philippines and Indonesia's historical, cultural and geographical ties as maritime neighbors and founding members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

They also recalled the outcomes of the 8th Joint Commission on Bilateral Cooperation held in Jakarta on April 23, 2026, and reaffirmed their commitment to strengthen cooperation in political and economic affairs, maritime security, border management, boundary delimitation, legal and consular matters, development in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM), and people-to-people relations.

The two foreign ministers agreed to expedite the adoption of a new five-year Philippines-Indonesia Plan of Action to serve as a framework for further strengthening their partnership and advancing regional peace, stability and prosperity.

They also exchanged views on regional and global issues, particularly within ASEAN and the United Nations, including efforts to address transboundary haze and make meaningful progress on the situation in Myanmar.
Lazaro likewise welcomed Indonesia's continued support for the Philippines' ASEAN chairship ahead of the 49th ASEAN Summit this month.
Both officials underscored their shared commitment to preserving ASEAN unity and centrality in addressing regional challenges. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Study: Grads earn more when jobs match academic training
articles.summary: Graduates tend to earn more when their jobs match their academic training, according to a study conducted by the Philippine Institute for Development Studies.

blocks.text: November 3, 2026 | 12:00am
Job seekers fill out application forms at a job fair in Manila, Feb. 24, 2023.
Philippine Star / Edd Gumban
MANILA, Philippines — Graduates tend to earn more when their jobs match their academic training, according to a study conducted by the Philippine Institute for Development Studies.

The PIDS study – Labor Market Outcomes of Education Graduates in the Philippines: The Role of Licensure Credentials and Job Matching – also showed that licensure alone was not significantly associated with higher wages.

It is authored by PIDS research specialist Anna Rita Vargas, research analyst Paola Ellaine Luzon and senior research fellow Connie Bayudan-Dacuycuy, who examined the labor market outcomes of Filipinos aged 22 to 60 with bachelor’s degrees in education science and related fields.

Using data from the July 2024 round of the merged Labor Force Survey-Annual Poverty Indicators Survey, the researchers analyzed outcomes among education graduates with or without professional licenses.
The study’s weighted estimates represented approximately 1.83 million graduates nationwide.

The authors said among licensed graduates, the predicted probability of underemployment was 3.98 percent for those in public-sector employment, compared with 14.73 percent for those in private-sector employment or who are self-employed.
The researchers recommended aligning curricula and licensure preparation with labor market needs and strengthening career pathways for licensed and unlicensed education graduates.
The PIDS added that the relationship between licensure and wages also varies by employment sector.
In particular, the results suggest that the financial benefits associated with licensure differ between those employed in government or government-controlled corporations and those working elsewhere.

“These findings mean that having a professional license does not automatically translate into higher pay. While a license can demonstrate professional qualifications and help graduates qualify for certain jobs, their earnings also depend on whether their work matches their training and the sector in which they are employed. The study identifies these relationships but does not establish that licensure or working in a particular sector directly causes higher earnings,” the study said.

articles.title: Philippines to host Quad leaders’ summit during ASEAN meet
articles.summary: The leaders of Australia, India, Japan and the United States will meet in Manila during the Nov. 15-18 Association of Southeast Asian Nations conference, the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue’s…

blocks.text: November 3, 2026 | 12:00am
Workers assemble an archway in front of the Philippine International Convention Center in Pasay yesterday for the 49th ASEAN Summit.
Edd Gumban

MANILA, Philippines — The leaders of Australia, India, Japan and the United States will meet in Manila during the Nov. 15-18 Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) conference, the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue’s first leaders’ summit since 2024, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed.
The summit would be the first for US President Donald Trump in his current term.
“We will have a Quad leaders’ meeting in Manila in the – I guess today is the 31st – next month,” Rubio said on Saturday on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Atlanta, Georgia.
The Philippines chairs the ASEAN this year and will host the leaders’ summit and other meetings from Nov. 16 to 18.

The Quad group is a key strategic partnership for cooperation on maritime security. It aims to promote a “free and open” Indo-Pacific and balance China’s expanding military and economic influence in the area.
During the G20 gathering, Rubio said the world is seeing concerning attacks in the South China Sea and the Strait of Taiwan that put economies in danger.
He stressed that one of the most severe consequences to sea lanes being under attack or under coercion is the rise of food security problems.
The foreign ministers of Quad nations remain seriously concerned about the situation in the East China Sea and the South China Sea and the militarization of disputed features.

In a statement during the Quad Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in New Delhi in May, the Quad reiterated its strong opposition to any destabilizing or unilateral actions, including by force or coercion, that threaten peace and stability in the region.
Ironclad
Meanwhile, US Ambassador Lee Lipton described Washington’s commitment to Philippine security as “ironclad,” following the visit of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in Cebu last week.

Lipton said Hegseth’s leadership of the Department of War and his frequent engagements with the US’s partners in Southeast Asia demonstrate the Trump administration’s determination to strengthen alliances, deepen regional cooperation and ensure that peace is backed by strength.

“As we mark 75 years of the US-Philippines Mutual Defense Treaty, our message is clear: our alliance is stronger than ever,” Lipton said. “We stand firmly with the Filipino people in defending sovereignty, protecting territorial integrity and upholding the freedom of navigation on which we all rely for vibrant global commerce.”

“The United States is proud to call the Philippines an ally, partner and friend. Our relationship is not simply a matter of treaties or shared strategic interests; it is a bond between our peoples that grows stronger every day,” he added. — Roel Pareño

articles.title: DepEd prioritizes violence-hit campuses in hiring counselor associates
articles.summary: The Department of Education is conducting risk assessments to prioritize large schools and those with a history of violence in the hiring and deployment of school counselor associates amid budget…

blocks.text: November 3, 2026 | 12:00am
This file photo shows a facade of the Department of Education.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Education (DepEd) is conducting risk assessments to prioritize large schools and those with a history of violence in the hiring and deployment of school counselor associates amid budget constraints, Education Secretary Sonny Angara said.

“Every year we are given a budget for the hiring of counselor associates. We distribute it for the 40,000-plus schools based on risk and usually, we have a risk assessment. Usually, incidents of bullying and violence tend to happen in bigger schools, in schools in urban areas. So, those schools that have a history, we will really provide them counselor associates,” Angara said.
The DepEd aims to complete the hiring of 10,000 school counselor associates by the end of 2026.
Angara noted that only 5,000 of the more than 45,000 schools nationwide have registered guidance counselors.

“What we hope is that we hire a combination of guidance counselors and have school counselor associates. Not a full-fledged guidance counselor, but with experience or units in psychology, in behavioral science, so will be able to spot any mental health issues and be able to guide our students,” he added.
Angara said the hiring is timely amid increasing incidents of bullying, school violence, mental health issues and depression among learners.
The DepEd is also seeking an additional P147.9 billion from the Senate to fund important programs left unfunded under its proposed P975.96-billion allocation for 2027.
“If you look at the most successful countries with the most successful education systems, they tend to spend more on education,” Angara said.
He admitted, however, that securing the additional funding would be a long shot.

“It is a long shot… but it’s a shot we have to take because it’s our duty. I think the fact that the senators are asking what are the most important items for us, I think that’s an indication that they really want to, at least at a minimum level, restore some of the budget that was taken away and fund other programs that may not be funded anymore,” he added.

articles.title: Nearly 90% in Yolanda mass grave identified
articles.summary: After more than a decade of having nameless crosses in a lonely field, victims buried in the Yolanda mass grave may finally have their names in their resting places.

blocks.text: November 3, 2026 | 12:00am

Following the completion of DNA analysis, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Regional Office VIII has announced a breakthrough: nearly 90 percent of the victims buried in the mass grave have been identified.
PNA / File photo
TACLOBAN CITY, Philippines — After more than a decade of having nameless crosses in a lonely field, victims buried in the Yolanda mass grave may finally have their names in their resting places.

Results of the disaster victim identification are expected to be released on Nov. 8, before the 13th anniversary of Super Typhoon Yolanda’s onslaught, according to NBI Region VIII director Jeremy Lotoc.
For 13 years, over 2,200 deceased have lain in the mass grave at the Holy Cross Memorial in Barangay Basper, Tacloban City.
“These are not just numbers. They are mothers, fathers, children, whose families have been waiting for 13 long years to know where their loved ones are,” Lotoc said.
Once released, the disaster victim identification results will be turned over to Tacloban officials, aiding in the restructuring of the crosses and tombs.

“From nameless graves to named memories – after 13 years of waiting, grieving and hoping, justice and closure may finally come for the thousands who perished in one of the country’s darkest days,” Lotoc added.
About 6,300 people, mostly in Eastern Visayas, died in the onslaught of Yolanda, marking it as one of the deadliest natural calamities in Philippine history.
Tacloban was its ground zero, wherein more than 2,000 residents were killed by the super typhoon and its devastating storm surges that swallowed entire communities.

Thirteen years later, the mass grave in Barangay Basper remains more than just a burial ground – it stands as a sacred place of remembrance, a silent witness to the lives lost and the pain that still lingers.
For families mourning relatives who were never found or identified, the site is where prayers are whispered, candles are lit and memories are kept alive.
Each name remembered is a promise that even after over a decade, Tacloban will never forget.

articles.title: Gas prices going up, diesel down today
articles.summary: Gasoline prices are set to rise while diesel and kerosene are headed for a rollback.

blocks.text: November 3, 2026 | 12:00am
Motorists queue at a gasoline station in Quezon City on July 7, 2024.
STAR / Miguel De Guzman
MANILA, Philippines — Gasoline prices are set to rise while diesel and kerosene are headed for a rollback.
The Department of Energy (DOE) yesterday announced an increase of up to P3.50 per liter in gasoline prices, effective today.
Diesel and kerosene prices, meanwhile, will go down by at least P1 and P1.90 per liter, respectively.
Diesel prices declined as the supply outlook improved following stock releases, Chinese exports and higher Russian diesel shipments, local industry sources said.
Asian gasoline supplies, however, remained tight despite the release of Chinese export quotas, as higher crude import costs weighed on regional refining margins.
Refined petroleum products largely tracked crude oil movements last week, with prices remaining supported by concerns over potential disruptions to energy supplies in the Middle East.
Markets also remained cautious amid fears of a possible escalation of tensions in the region following the US midterm elections.
In the Philippines, the national average fuel inventory stood at 52.95 days as of Oct. 30, latest DOE data showed.

Broken down by product, diesel stocks were sufficient for 56.66 days, gasoline for 52.29 days, kerosene for 148.55 days, jet fuel for 58.88 days, fuel oil for 63.3 days and liquefied petroleum gas for 35.12 days.

articles.title: SC urges public to be cautious in expressing views
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has urged the public to exercise caution when expressing views on current and social issues and sharing information to avoid facing possible criminal charges.

blocks.text: November 3, 2026 | 12:00am

In its “Legally Speaking” series on Facebook, the high tribunal discussed legal terms such as libel, slander and slander by deed, as well as legal principles that may serve as defenses in cases involving freedom of expression.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — The Supreme Court (SC) has urged the public to exercise caution when expressing views on current and social issues and sharing information to avoid facing possible criminal charges.
These include the “doctrine of fair comment,” which may be invoked as a defense against libel cases filed by public officials or personalities, “privileged communication” and “prior restraint.”
The SC stressed that the Philippines upholds the democratic rights to free speech, freedom of the press and freedom of expression.
“Whether you are a broadcaster, a vlogger, a writer or an ordinary citizen, remember that every right has a corresponding responsibility,” it said.

Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen, who is among the contenders for the next chief justice post, has also written SC majority decisions addressing issues involving free speech, emphasizing that the Constitution protects this right.

articles.title: DOH advises public against relying solely on water filters
articles.summary: The Department of Health has advised the public against relying entirely on water filtration devices to ensure safe drinking water as the country prepares for the effects of the impending super El…

blocks.text: November 3, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Health (DOH) has advised the public against relying entirely on water filtration devices to ensure safe drinking water as the country prepares for the effects of the impending super El Niño.
The DOH recommended pretreating raw water containing debris, organic matter and suspended solids to prevent filtration systems from getting clogged and ensure their effectiveness.

“Pretreatment can be undertaken if the raw water is highly contaminated and has debris, organic matter and suspended solids to prevent the filters from getting clogged,” Health Assistant Secretary Tagumpay Maniquis said.
He explained that a filter’s ability to remove contaminants depends on its size, noting that filters with a 0.1-micron capacity cannot remove contaminants smaller than that measurement.
“To deactivate viruses or bacteria less than 0.1 micron, you can boil the water or use a disinfectant. What is commonly used for disinfection is a chlorine tablet,” Maniquis said.
The DOH advised the public to coordinate with their local health offices on the proper use of chlorine tablets.

For those using water filtration systems to improve drinking water quality, the agency also reminded the public to check whether their devices are registered with the Food and Drug Administration (FDA).
“It should have undergone registration and been issued a certificate of health-related device registration,” Maniquis said.
The registration status of water filters and other treatment devices can be verified through the FDA’s online portal at https://verification.fda.gov.ph.
School gardens

In the education sector, Education Secretary Sonny Angara has directed schools to strengthen the planting of drought-tolerant and short-cycle crops to ensure the uninterrupted implementation of the government’s feeding program despite the threat of El Niño.

“We must be prepared and resourceful in the face of the challenges brought by El Niño. Under the administration of President Marcos, it is our priority to ensure that nutritional support for our students remains uninterrupted,” Angara said.
He stressed that protecting school gardens is essential to the government’s efforts to strengthen food security, mitigate hunger and promote child welfare.
Angara directed schools to adjust their crop selection and soil management systems to address prolonged dry spells, extreme heat and water shortages that could disrupt conventional planting cycles.
He recommended fast-growing, drought-resistant and nutrient-rich crops such as munggo, okra, malunggay, saluyot, alugbati and kamote.
Schools were also instructed to adopt water-saving measures, including organic mulching, rainwater harvesting, alternate-day watering schedules and drip irrigation.

For urban and space-constrained schools, the Department of Education will issue standardized guidelines for non-soil and vertical farming systems, including container gardening, hydroponics and stacked planting.

“This is more than just planting vegetables; we are teaching our youth about resilience and cooperation, while ensuring that there is sufficient, nutritious food on every table in our schools,” Angara said.

“With the help of our teachers, parents and local governments, we are strengthening our gardens to serve as a guide and a source of support during times of drought. Together, we are fostering the future of our youth,” he added.
Price control

Meanwhile, Sen. Francis Pangilinan has called on the government to strictly enforce price freezes and jail major hoarders who may exploit the impending El Niño crisis, warning of its potential impact on food production and consumer prices.

Pangilinan, chairman of the Senate committee on agriculture, food and agrarian reform, said government crackdowns should target the masterminds behind agricultural cartels rather than low-level market retailers. — Neil Jayson Servallos, Bella Cariaso

articles.title: PNP monitors transport hubs
articles.summary: The Philippine National Police is maintaining heightened operational readiness and road safety across major transport hubs and primary highways as millions of Filipinos return to urban centers after…

blocks.text: November 3, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine National Police (PNP) is maintaining heightened operational readiness and road safety across major transport hubs and primary highways as millions of Filipinos return to urban centers after All Saints’ and All Souls’ Days.

PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. directed all police regional offices to sustain foot and mobile patrols, man assist desks and monitor high-density choke points to deter opportunistic criminals and prevent vehicular accidents.

Nartatez noted that the extended security drive aligns with the directives of President Marcos and Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla to safeguard the traveling public, prevent crime and manage traffic flow.

“As travelers make their way back to their homes, schools and workplaces, the PNP remains fully mobilized to keep roads secure, maintain public order and respond swiftly to any incident that may disrupt travel,” Nartatez said. “Our priority is to ensure that every Filipino reaches their destination safely.”
Under the directive, police presence will remain concentrated in bus terminals, commercial seaports, airports, train stations and transport interchanges.

The instruction comes after massive crowds observed Undas, with data showing that over 1.16 million visitors gathered in Manila’s two largest public cemeteries alone on Nov. 1, alongside millions more who paid respects to deceased loved ones in provincial cemeteries nationwide.
Nartatez urged long-distance drivers and private vehicle owners to adhere to traffic laws, avoid distracted driving and practice rest stops to prevent fatigue-related road crashes.

“No destination is worth risking lives for,” Nartatez stressed. “We urge motorists to follow traffic laws, avoid speeding, never drive under the influence of alcohol, refrain from using mobile phones while driving and take adequate rest before long trips.”

“As we conclude this meaningful observance, let us carry home not only cherished memories of our loved ones but also a renewed commitment to protect one another through responsible and law-abiding behavior,” he said.
Fewer bus travelers
The Philippine Bus Operators Association of the Philippines (PBOAP) has reported fewer bus travelers during Undas compared to last year.
“There weren’t that many queues in bus terminals. It’s also observable that there are less travelers now,” PBOAP executive director Alex Yague said.

Yague said passengers may have taken advantage of the long weekend to spread out their trips over several days, allowing passenger traffic to be distributed over four to five days and ease the usual surge of travel demand during Undas.
PBOAP noted that another factor in the fewer bus travelers is the increase in private vehicles traveling to provinces.

“Maybe because the fares and tolls have been expensive. Friends and other passengers may have done carpooling, while others might have their pasalubong delivered to their loved ones in the province,” Yague said.
Despite the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board approving over a thousand special bus permits, Yague said passenger figures have not exhausted the travel demand this year.
PBOAP said Undas travel now had a lot of advantages, including good weather and road conditions for faster bus turnarounds.
No major accidents have been recorded over the weekend, Yague said.
Meanwhile, Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon has ordered the Metro Rail Transit Line 3 (MRT-3) to deploy additional trains to assist at least 6,000 more commuters back to the metro.
According to MRT-3, 19 trains were deployed yesterday in anticipation of the expected increase in passengers returning home after Undas.
From Oct. 29 to Nov. 2, the Philippine Red Cross attended to 8,721 patients — Andrew Ronquillo, Rhodina Villanueva

articles.title: LTFRB fines Move It P555.7 million over excess riders
articles.summary: Ride-hailing app Move It PH has been ordered by the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board to pay a staggering P555.7-million fine for onboarding motorcycle riders beyond the…

blocks.text: November 3, 2026 | 12:00am
In this handout photo, a Move It rider waits at a crossing in Bonifacio Global City, Taguig.
Move It

MANILA, Philippines — Ride-hailing app Move It PH has been ordered by the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) to pay a staggering P555.7-million fine for onboarding motorcycle riders beyond the government-authorized cap.?
In a document obtained by The STAR, LTFRB Chairman Greg Pua said Move It PH was found administratively liable for violating the rider allocation established under the Motorcycle Taxi Pilot Program.?
Across areas of operation in Metro Manila, Cebu and Cagayan de Oro, the total Move it PH active riders as of May accounted for 73,321, a breach of the 17,746 authorized allocation by LTFRB.
The LTFRB has imposed a P10,000 administrative fine for each of the 55,575 rider-partner maintained in excess of the authorized allocation.
Failure to pay the fine may lead to a suspension of Move It PH’s authority to participate in the program and revocation of its accreditation.

“The foregoing figures show that respondent exceeded its authorized allocation by 55,575 rider-partners, or more than three times the number it was expressly authorized to maintain under the MC Taxi-TWG’s Order (in 2025),” the decision read.?
The LTFRB also flagged Move It PH for its “disregard of the one-year temporary moratorium” on new riders’ onboarding.?

According to Move It PH, it adopted an internal classification on their rider-partners, including the distinction between full-time and part-time, online and offline riders and riders operating for more than or fewer than eight hours per day.?
However, the LTFRB maintained that its resolution “expressly fixed the number of rider-partners that respondent was authorized to maintain.”?
“To adopt respondent’s interpretation would effectively permit every regulated entity to redefine the scope of its regulatory obligations through unilateral operational policies,” said the LTFRB.

“(The penalty) is proportionate to the gravity and magnitude of the violation and is reasonably calculated to secure compliance with lawful regulatory directives and preserve the integrity of the Motorcycle Taxi Pilot Program,” the LTFRB board said.

articles.title: Groups call for de-escalation of tension with China
articles.summary: A coalition of 23 business and sectoral groups is calling for de-escalation of tensions between the Philippines and China, citing risks to deep trade and economic ties if strained relations persist.

blocks.text: November 3, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — A coalition of 23 business and sectoral groups is calling for de-escalation of tensions between the Philippines and China, citing risks to deep trade and economic ties if strained relations persist.

“We respectfully appeal to Philippine and Chinese authorities to lower the temperature, restore disciplined diplomatic engagement and build a stable, respectful and productive bilateral relationship,” the groups said in a joint statement, amid heightened heated exchanges between the Chinese embassy in Manila and some Philippine officials.

The groups include the Employers Confederation of the Philippines, Foundation for Economic Freedom, Federation of Filipino-Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry Inc., Foreign Buyers Association of the Philippines, Philippine Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Philippine Exporters Confederation Inc., Philippine Hotel Owners Association Inc. and Semiconductor and Electronic Industries in the Philippines Foundation Inc.
With the prevailing global uncertainty and supply chain disruptions, the groups called for a careful approach in handling the two countries’ relations, while advancing national interests.

“All parties should avoid inflammatory rhetoric, public recriminations and social media exchanges that could further strain bilateral relations. Diplomacy is best pursued through established channels, coordinated institutions, informed dialogue, mutual respect and a clear understanding of national interests,” the groups said.
Given the deep trade and economic ties between the two countries, the groups cited the importance of a foreign policy that protects sovereignty, economic security and long-term development.

Citing data from the Philippine Statistics Authority, the groups said that China and Hong Kong serve as the Philippines’ largest trading partner, accounting for nearly 30 percent of the country’s total international trade in recent years. The Philippines accounts for less than one percent of China’s total global trade.
Deeply connected
The two economies are deeply connected in terms of trade, manufacturing, construction, infrastructure, agriculture, retail, energy, electric vehicles, solar panels and other sectors.

China is also a major supplier of essential goods, industrial inputs, machinery, electronics, strategic raw materials and renewable-energy technologies needed by Philippine businesses, consumers and even the country’s clean-energy transition.

“Because trade with China represents a far greater share of Philippine external trade than the Philippine market represents of China’s global trade, we must practice careful economic statecraft while pursuing strategic diversification, stronger domestic industries, local assembly and manufacturing and sound diplomacy,” the groups said.
Beyond trade, the Philippines also benefits from remittances from overseas Filipino workers in China, Hong Kong and Macau, according to the business groups.

“Whatever our political differences or maritime disputes, constructive diplomacy and stable economic relations are essential to protecting livelihoods, maintaining investor confidence, controlling costs, accelerating clean-energy adoption and sustaining development,” the groups said.
As the Philippines aims to attract regional tourism, investment and other commercial opportunities, the groups also emphasized the need for a competitive, predictable and welcoming environment.
As such, the groups urged both the Philippines and China to avoid statements that heighten tensions.
Coherent foreign policy needed

The groups also urged both parties to strengthen and pursue a centralized, coherent and consistent foreign policy by having designated authorities communicate their position through coordinated institutions and established channels.

They likewise called on the parties to uphold sovereignty, while preserving economic cooperation. This can be done by defending sovereign rights under international law, while maintaining dialogue and cooperation on trade, investment, tourism, energy security, electric mobility, solar deployment and other areas of mutual interests.

They also cited the need for both countries to prioritize trade, investment as well as the creation of decent work by expanding market access, strengthening resilience of supply chains, promoting technology transfer, encouraging local production, clean energy generation, as well as investments.
The groups said mutual respect and responsible communication should take preeminence over public exchanges that intensify tensions between the two countries.

“Constructive relations with China do not require abandoning Philippine sovereignty, overlooking legitimate concerns or compromising an independent foreign policy. Effective diplomacy means defending national interests while avoiding unnecessary escalation,” the groups said.
They also maintained that firmness and friendship, vigilance and cooperation, as well as national dignity and economic pragmatism can go hand in hand.

While protecting the country’s sovereignty is important, the groups stressed that Filipinos also need a government that works to expand prosperity to allow entrepreneurs, farmers, manufacturers, workers and consumers to benefit.

“For the Philippines, the path forward must be one of sobriety, strategic clarity, economic pragmatism and constructive engagement with China and the wider international community,” their joint statement read. “Our national interest demands nothing less.”

articles.title: What might Trump have planned for Iran following the midterm election?
articles.summary: While the US midterms could open a window for diplomacy with Iran, they could also unleash a new military escalation. DW spoke with analysts to identify eight factors that could tip the balance…

image.caption: The Reuters news agency cited three senior Iranian officials and an additional source as saying that Iran has deliberately prolonged talks to weaken Trump politicallyImage: Brendan Smialowski/AFP

blocks.text: The US Republican Party is entering the midterm elections with Donald Trump's administration seemingly unable to either win or diplomatically resolve the Iran war. If the Republicans lose control of the US Congress, the administration will have to navigate an entirely different political landscape for the rest of Trump's second term, but the course of the war is not decided just in Washington — or in Tehran.

Seeking to identify key factors that could tip the balance towards war or peace in Iran, DW spoke with Omid Memarian of DAWN, a Washington-based think tank focused on reforming the US's Middle East policy; the Finland-based political scientist Leila Morovati; and Babak Rezaeedaryakenari, a professor of international relations at Leiden University in the Netherlands.
1. US midterms: Is Trump set for more scrutiny?

A Democratic victory would push Trump to focus more on domestic issues and would likely expose the financial costs of the war in the US Congress, Memarian told DW. However, Trump could continue limited strikes on Iran without formally declaring war.
Memarian said Trump would seek a way out that "saves face" after Tuesday's election.
With Trump, Memarian said, Iran is engaged in a "big gamble with someone who does not behave like a conventional politician." This increases the risk of renewed attacks.
How serious are Iran's new threats of retaliation?

Rezaeedaryakenari made a similar point: "The president has broad authority and freedom of action, especially in foreign policy and the conduct of military operations. A Republican defeat, even with increased pressure from Congress, doesn't necessarily stop new attacks."
2. Deadlock in Israel puts pressure on Netanyahu

Israel's October 27 election ended in deadlock. Neither the coalition around incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, nor the camp supporting former IDF chief Gadi Eisenkot managed to secure an outright majority.

Memarian said the political uncertainty could push Netanyahu to act on major decisions while he still wields power — making the transition period the "most fragile and dangerous" for renewed escalation.
No clear winner emerges in Israel's election

A change of government in Israel would not fundamentally alter Israel's Iran policy, Memarian said. Netanyahu's main rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, "may be more deferential to America" and coordinate more closely with Washington. But ties with Trump are personal, and Eisenkot "certainly won't be like Netanyahu, who could sell any plan or scenario to Trump."

Rezaeedaryakenari said Israel's security concerns about Iran "are not limited to Netanyahu himself." A new government could change the timing of a confrontation and coordination with Washington, but the security establishment and ruling coalition would also shape the risk of an attack, he said.
3. Nuclear impasse: 'The ladder of tension'
Iran's nuclear program remains the biggest open issue between the governments, with the US rejecting the Iranian narrative that the program is meant only for civilian use.
But the two sides are also at odds on how the talks themselves should be set up, Memarian said.
"The US wants negotiations to start not only with a focus on Iran's nuclear program, but with concessions right at the outset," he said.
Iran seeks the lifting of sanctions and the release of frozen assets before nuclear talks begin. If the sides don't move closer, Memarian warns, the odds of a renewed war rise.
Until the sides agree on an agenda, Memarian said, they are likely to keep "climbing the ladder of tension."

Morovati, a Finland-based political analyst, said the nuclear program was "the crux" of the standoff. Iran's government sees it as a survival guarantee and bargaining chip, she said. In turn, Washington fears that a nuclear Iran would upend its security calculations and long-term strategy for the Middle East and beyond, which is why it insists on putting the issue on the table first.
4. Strait of Hormuz: Is Iran's leverage also a risk factor?

Before the United States and Israel launched the war in late February, about 20% of the world's oil passed through the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has since drastically cut on the energy exports through the naval chokepoint, using at as leverage on US and Israel.
But, Memarian said, Iran's restrictions in the strait won't trigger escalation on their own.

Should US officials decide that a broader attack is needed to change Iran's calculations, any incident could serve as a pretext, Memarian said. If Washington considers the risks too high, it may opt for an economic blockade while keeping negotiations on the table. In that scenario, "even occasional tensions in the Strait of Hormuz won't pull America into war," according to the US-based analyst.
5. The Houthis in Yemen: Iran's allies, not subordinates

The Houthi rebels in Yemen have also been targeting energy exports on the Red Sea — including attacks on Saudi cities and infrastructure. But Memarian notes the Yemeni rebels' roots and struggle are "entirely domestic and organic" despite their ideological closeness to Tehran.
Memarian said the Houthis made "pragmatic calculations" and their actions did not necessarily translate into an escalation between Iran and the United States.
Still, the United States could use the rebels' action as a pretext to strike Iran again.
More fighting between Yemen's Houthis, Saudi Arabia

Rezaeedaryakenari offered a slightly different assessment. Houthi attacks on shipping and on countries in the region, he says, "can both widen the war and accelerate coalition-building against the Islamic Republic." Countries that don't want war with Tehran "may turn to closer military cooperation to protect their trade and security." That doesn't necessarily mean entering the war directly, he adds, "but it could narrow the Islamic Republic's room for maneuver."
6. Regional mediators: Four countries with a lot at stake

With direct talks between the governments of Iran and the United States stalled, the world turned its attention to Qatar, Oman, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia. While each nation plays a different role in the crisis, they all have a direct stake in ending the war.
"They are close to the US, but also want to maintain ties with Iran and build regional alliances to prevent future conflicts," Memarian said.
Morovati said the failure of the United States to support its Arab allies during the war could eventually push them to reconsider their policies and turn to the US's rivals.
7. What will Trump administration do after the election?

During the campaign, Trump said he expected a deal with Iran soon after the midterm elections. Meanwhile, the Reuters news agency cited three senior Iranian officials and an additional source as saying that Tehran has deliberately prolonged talks to weaken Trump politically.

Memarian said Iran's leaders believed that a Republican defeat would increase pressure on Trump to end the war. But Trump will remain the key foreign policy decision-maker, and congressional pressure is unlikely to play a deciding role.
He said the present moment offers the "best opportunity" to end the standoff before Trump leaves office in January 2029.
"Iran's leaders need to think about their endgame," Memarian said, warning that Trump could launch a massive attack, inflict serious damage and then declare victory.
Iran conflict: Could a new phase of the war be imminent?
Rezaeedaryakenari said "escalatory factors" would have the upper hand in the coming months — and the likelihood of a military escalation is high.

Iran's government can only avert a new round of war with a fundamental policy shift and concessions that the country's leaders would consider close to surrender. However, he said, such a retreat would also threaten the regime's survival by weakening its ideological justification and eroding support.
8. Economic toll: Warring parties not at breaking point
High oil prices, shipping risks and economic strain are putting pressure on all sides as the war enters its ninth month. Could that push Tehran, Washington and regional capitals toward compromise?
"The economy is the Achilles' heel of every party to this war," Morovati said, "and that holds even for countries beyond the region."
Energy prices as a source of pressure on the US government, Morovati said.
"We've seen that energy supply and the expectations of the American public have been influential," Morovati said, "and this is one of the problems the Trump administration faces."
At the same time, Morovati said, Arab countries do not act as a united bloc toward Tehran.
"If they come under severe security and economic pressure, they may take joint action, but so far that hasn't happened in practice," Morovati said.
What now for Saudi Arabia after Riyadh airport attack?
Memarian also sees the economic costs as an incentive for a deal. But he also claims that each side believes that inflicting more pain on the other will strengthen its hand in future talks.
"That can easily turn this into a war of attrition, and in recent months that has been the approach," Memarian said. Neither side has yet reached the point where it sees compromise as unavoidable.
